title: The native Web path sustains one rendered, durable DSH conversation.
given: G1 through G4 hold, a model is configured, and the human selects a workspace.
when: The human launches dsh web and submits two sequential prompts in the same browser session.
expect: One DSH host admits both prompts to the same session, the second turn can derive the first turn's history, canonical events render in the browser, and the conversation remains durable.
notes: The four child branches prove composition, browser boot, repeated interaction, and core execution. G0 must still be verified independently.

children.title: The Web profile composes one long-lived host and agent runtime.
children.given: G1.1 through G1.4 hold.
children.when: runProfile() receives the Web boot request.
children.expect: One Cordis root owns the agent runtime and Web host services until the foreground process shuts down.
children.notes: This path has no SDK parent-child JSON-RPC boundary.

children.title: dsh web selects the shipped Web profile.
children.given: The DSH CLI is installed and receives a valid web subcommand.
children.when: The CLI parser resolves the subcommand.
children.expect: It produces the same request as --profile web and forwards Web arguments.
children.notes: The alias is explicit rather than inferred from a frontend entry.

children.title: The Web profile stacks base, Web, and override layers.
children.given: The Web profile is absent or contains its shipped bundle roster.
children.when: Profile discovery initializes or loads the roster.
children.expect: dsh-base applies first, dsh-web-app applies next, and user overlays remain above both.
children.notes: Base contributes the runtime. Web contributes host, transport, and browser rows.

children.title: Boot mounts and audits the complete Cordis tree.
children.given: The composed patch stack resolves and every required package is available.
children.when: boot() mounts Loader and waits for settlement.
children.expect: Every entry becomes active or startup fails with the responsible plugin error.
children.notes: Dependency injection, not YAML order, controls activation.

children.title: dsh-base supplies the harness capabilities.
children.given: The base bundle patch is the first profile layer.
children.when: Its rows join the empty Cordis deployment.
children.expect: The deployment gains sessions, persistence, metering, compaction, tools, agent loop, policy, and model adapters.
children.notes: The Web bundle does not reimplement these services.

children.title: The browser UI is a projection of the live host composition.
children.given: G2.1 through G2.4 hold.
children.when: A browser requests the native DSH URL.
children.expect: The browser activates the client plugins belonging to the current host deployment and mounts a resident session surface.
children.notes: The static Vite shell is incomplete until the host injects its boot graph.

children.title: The native host serves API routes and the SPA fallback.
children.given: The Web profile mounts the HTTP server and Web application glue.
children.when: An HTTP request reaches the bound route table.
children.expect: Named routes own API and plugin requests while the frontend owner serves unmatched SPA paths.
children.notes: The server is a browser carrier and owns no agent semantics.

children.title: The Web bundle mounts the frontend and publishes its URL.
children.given: The server is bound and the packaged frontend exists.
children.when: dsh-web-app.apply() activates.
children.expect: It mounts the frontend, publishes runtime facts, prints the URL, and optionally opens the browser.
children.notes: Browser opening waits for the Loader tree to settle.

children.title: The host derives a browser graph from live Loader entries.
children.given: Mounted packages may publish a built dsh.client face.
children.when: The module registry scans host Loader entries and transforms the served index.
children.expect: The page receives a validated boot graph and same-origin routes for each client bundle.
children.notes: The graph is the wire source of truth for the browser roster.

children.title: The browser builds and audits its Cordis client tree.
children.given: The page contains the bootstrap facade, boot graph, and loadable bundles.
children.when: AppWebEntry.run() creates a browser Context.
children.expect: Every client entry activates or fails visibly before the UI renderer receives the root element.
children.notes: This resident tree owns the browser session experience.

children.title: One browser session can carry multiple conversation rounds.
children.given: G3.1 through G3.5 hold and one workspace-backed browser Session remains selected.
children.when: The human submits a prompt, observes its completion, and submits a second prompt in the same composer.
children.expect: Both submissions use the same session ID, each reaches the DSH Agent, both turns appear in the same conversation, and input remains available afterward.
children.notes: This is the explicit multi-round proof that the previous Web presentation lacked.

children.title: The composer settles each submission back into an input-ready state.
children.given: A session input shell owns a non-empty draft and no submission is already in flight.
children.when: The submission succeeds.
children.expect: The draft commits, the machine returns to plain, and the same shell can begin another submission.
children.notes: Keyboard input therefore has a repeated landing point.

children.title: The browser Session turns each submission into a typed prompt call.
children.given: A browser Session exists and the composer supplies content.
children.when: Session.prompt() receives queue or steer input.
children.expect: It calls api.sessions.prompt with its stable session ID, content, mode, and browser time zone.
children.notes: The UI never reaches into the host Agent registry directly.

children.title: The browser carrier separates prompt admission from event delivery.
children.given: The page passed the trust fence and its connection generation is active.
children.when: The browser performs an API operation and runs its event loops.
children.expect: Unary calls use HTTP while host and session facts arrive through reconnecting downlink streams.
children.notes: The browser does not wait on one giant request to observe a turn.

children.title: The API proxy admits content to a live or resumable Agent.
children.given: The session resolves to an Agent, content is valid, and prompt mode is supported.
children.when: The host handles session.prompt.
children.expect: It creates one durable user message and sends it through followup() or steer().
children.notes: The resolver can reuse a live Agent or resume persisted history.

children.title: Runtime events update the same browser session mirror.
children.given: The mux stream is subscribed and the DSH Session emits canonical events.
children.when: The API proxy pushes session frames.
children.expect: The browser repairs gaps, derives the next conversation snapshot, and notifies the rendered UI.
children.notes: The browser mirror is live state, while the Session log remains authority.

children.title: DSH core executes and preserves every admitted turn.
children.given: G4.1 through G4.4 hold.
children.when: An admitted user message enters the Agent inbox.
children.expect: The normal DSH turn machine reaches the provider, records canonical events, flushes durable history, and returns the Agent to idle.
children.notes: Web changes the interaction surface, not the Agent execution model.

children.title: The Agent inbox wakes the normal turn driver.
children.given: A live Agent is idle and its inbox receives an admitted message.
children.when: followup() targets a turn or steer() targets a step.
children.expect: The driver opens a turn, claims input, assembles prompts and tools, and advances the regular step machine.
children.notes: There is no Web-specific Agent class.

children.title: The configured adapter owns provider transport.
children.given: The route resolves, credentials exist, and the request fits provider capabilities.
children.when: The loop invokes the adapter's stream().
children.expect: The adapter sends the request, parses streaming output, and yields normalized DSH chunks.
children.notes: DeepSeek is native, while other adapters can satisfy the same seam.

children.title: The Session event log remains the shared source of truth.
children.given: The turn owns a DSH Session and runtime facts have canonical event forms.
children.when: The loop records input, steps, messages, tools, results, and turn completion.
children.expect: Model history, live updates, replay, resume, metering, compaction, and projections derive from one ordered log.
children.notes: The browser mirror never becomes durable authority.

children.title: Persistence preserves sessions across browser and host lifecycles.
children.given: The base profile mounts JSONL persistence and checkpoint policy.
children.when: A turn reaches a durability boundary or the host disposes.
children.expect: Events flush to the session root and later Web sessions can inspect or resume the history.
children.notes: Closing a browser tab does not define session truth.
